<thought>We need to determine how many methyl (CH₃) groups are present in the compound of the sample. The most direct way is to retrieve the 13C NMR spectrum for the sample and count the number of distinct carbon signals in the typical methyl region (≈10–30 ppm). This will give the number of unique CH₃ carbons. If no such signals are present, the answer is 0.</thought>
